close_reason: False alarm: cascade iterates top-down and each depth's retain only removes nodes at depth d, so any_parent reads from the already-updated tree at d-1. Correct behavior.
description: In chain_walk (lib.rs:2596-2648), §6.1.5(g)(iii)(2) cascade-deletion logic iterates d from 2..=leaf_depth, at each step collecting 'reachable' as the union of expected_policy_sets of all parents at depth d-1. However the any_parent variable (line 2640) does not filter to 'living' anyPolicy parents — it checks any anyPolicy node at parent_depth without verifying that anyPolicy node itself is reachable. In a multi-level tree where an anyPolicy node at depth k was previously deleted but the variable still reads the original slice, an orphaned anyPolicy could shadow the deletion and incorrectly preserve child nodes. This is a correctness risk on deep policy trees with anyPolicy at intermediate levels. The deletion pass does NOT update the slice before the next iteration — it calls tree.retain() in-place, so subsequent iterations within the same for-loop see the post-retain state. Verify whether the in-place retain makes the cascade correct or whether iteration order is still problematic for deep trees (>2 levels with anyPolicy at non-root depths).
title: pkix-path: §6.1.5(g) initial_policy_set intersection misses cascade-prune downward for multi-level trees
